sources.src: Item 271 (Justin 2026-10-20: "i think we need to reduce how much lightining is stacking and how much they give off, this room in inderdark is too bright. Maybe a by light source determination"): each light source burns by its own row on every floor but the planes, whatever its biome's share (the Underdark's 75%, the Caverns' 55%, the placed share below), falling off as the placed lights do: a candle a small pool well under a torch, a brazier the brightest placed light. of: the light kinds (prop ids, floor light kinds) the row is for.

placed.src: Item 247 (Justin 2026-10-20: i think the light from light sources is a bit too high, the crypt is too bright because of it): on these floors every placed light (torches, candles, braziers, the forge, beacons, the Crypt's green and violet torches, its mushroom, gas and ooze glows, the doors' spill) at this share; the hero's lamp, daylight, a body's own light and the things listed keep theirs. The Crypt's ambient was already about 15%: its unlit floor reads 0.135 to 0.150. Reach and falloff (Justin 2026-10-20: every room ends up being at max light in the crypt maybe the fall off of light needs to be more rapid?): each light at 0.7 of its reach, falling off as (1 - d / r) to the 2.6 (1.6 before), so the floor between two lights sits under the limit and the corners near the ambient

lip.src: Item 281 (Justin 2026-10-20: "the lighting here should show the lip of the lower row (otherwise it's impossible to find a door)"; "a south facing wall viewed from the north of it just shows up as black"): a wall one cell thick between two floors is drawn as a face looking south, and a face is lit from the floor at its foot, so seen from the north its coping (its top rows, the lip with its caps and doors) took none of the light of the floor beside it. The coping (rows: the top share of a face cell, the Dungeon's 29 of 128) takes at least share of the light of the floor north of it

flatCard.src: Item 280 (Justin 2026-10-20: "weird shadow on door frame"): a piece of wall drawn as a sprite (a front door, its arch and leaf in one picture) has no map of its own and is no body, so the card pass's form (its silhouette's slope, 1.7's for bodies and props) rounded its inner edge: the jamb beside a torch, its inner edge facing the doorway, took a dark crescent. These frames (their texture's frame name) are lit as a flat card, as the wall they stand in

stack.src: Item 271 (Justin 2026-10-20: "reduce how much lightining is stacking"): the placed lights on a pixel add as they are up to the knee, then ease toward the cap (cap - (cap - knee) e^-(sum - knee)/(cap - knee), by their brightest channel so a hue keeps), so a cluster of candles reads as one warm area; the hero's lamp and daylight add after, as they were

groundCover.note: 1.7 draws ground cover (moss, the moss bed under tall grass, ash, scorch, blood, bones, webs, water) as its own flat-lit pictures over the stone (surface.js:250 normal:false; vegart.js drawVegMoss), so the stone's relief does not show through it. The rewrite draws its paint and ground layers' alpha into a cover picture (puddles left out: Justin 2026-10-17, item 67, puddles keep their stone's relief) and takes share of the relief away under it.

grade.src: Item 254 (Justin 2026-10-20: post processing to make the visuals pop more, like increasing saturation; approved: a vibrance and contrast grade): the world's colour grade in the lit passes (light-glsl.js graded), the HUD untouched. Vibrance lifts a colour by this share of how dull it is, so strong ones keep theirs; contrast bends the light about the pivot, darks down and lights up (0.2, near this world's middle: a lit room's mean holds). An area row's own grade wins (areas.<name>.grade)
